html:
The Cree are one of the largest First Nations peoples of Canada, with homelands across the forests and plains from Quebec to the Rockies. They speak a group of Algonquian dialects and are closely related to the Innu and Naskapi.

Most Cree lived as hunters, trappers and fishers of the northern forest, moving in family groups with the seasons. When the Hudson's Bay Company set up posts on Hudson Bay after 1670, Cree hunters became its main trading partners and middlemen, and they moved west with the fur trade. Some, the Plains Cree, took up horses and the bison hunt. With the Assiniboine and Ojibwe they formed an alliance that historians call the Iron Confederacy.

Families of Cree women and European fur traders were among the roots of the Métis. In the 1870s many Cree nations signed the Numbered Treaties with Canada. Today more than 350,000 Cree live in Canada, with small communities in Montana. See also Woodland Cree.
